Model a Binary Outcome From Sequential Patterns

Source: R/pattern_outcome.R
pattern_outcome.Rd

Selects the n patterns most associated with a two-valued outcome and fits one logistic regression of the outcome on their presence. This reproduces codyna::analyze_outcome(): the same pattern discovery and filters, the same ranking, and the same model, so the coefficients agree. The result is a tidy table, one row per selected pattern.

Usage

pattern_outcome(
  x,
  outcome = "last_obs",
  type = c("ngram", "gapped", "repeated"),
  len = 1:2,
  gap = 1,
  min_freq = 5,
  min_support = 0.01,
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  contain = NULL,
  n = 10,
  priority = "chisq",
  desc = TRUE,
  occurrences = FALSE,
  adjust = NULL,
  adjust_length = FALSE,
  group = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  cols = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Sequence data, in any form accepted by extract_sequences(): prepared data, a long event log, a wide data frame, a netobject, netobject_group or tna model.

outcome

The outcome, with exactly two distinct values: the name of a column stored with the sequences (a covariate of a wide data frame or long event log, or of a network's metadata), or a vector with one value per sequence. Use a vector for a model that stores no covariates, such as a tna model. outcome = "last_obs" uses each sequence's last observed state as the outcome and removes the states that end some sequence from all sequences (the default, as in codyna; for data whose final state codes the outcome, such as an appended "pass" or "fail").

type, len, gap, min_freq, min_support, start, end, contain

Pattern definition and filters; see sequence_patterns(). The defaults are codyna's: len = 1:2, gap = 1, min_freq = 5, min_support = 0.01.

n

Number of patterns entered into the model. Default 10.

priority

Column(s) ranking the patterns for selection, applied in order: "chisq" (default), "p_value", "support", "n_sequences", "occurrences", "proportion", "lift", "length".

desc

Logical, recycled to priority: rank in descending order. Default TRUE.

occurrences

Logical. Enter each pattern as its number of occurrences in the sequence instead of presence (0/1). Default FALSE.

adjust

Optional character vector of covariate columns added to the model.

adjust_length

Logical. Also add the number of observed states per sequence as a covariate. Default FALSE (codyna does not).

group

Optional column identifying the actor (or other cluster) each sequence belongs to; adds a random intercept. Requires lme4.

reference

The reference outcome value; the odds ratios are for the other value. Default: the first value in sorted order.

ci_level

Confidence level of the Wald intervals. Default 0.95.

cols

State columns of a wide data frame; see extract_sequences().

...

Passed to extract_sequences(), e.g. actor, action and time for a long event log.

Value

A data.frame with one row per selected pattern, in the model's term order (pattern name): pattern, length, occurrences, n_sequences, support, lift (as in sequence_patterns()), the support within each outcome value (support_<value>), chisq (the selection statistic), estimate (log odds ratio, adjusted for the other terms), std_error, ci_lower, ci_upper, p_value (Wald z), odds_ratio, or_lower, or_upper.

Conditions: nestimate_bad_input for a missing column, an outcome without exactly two values, or an unknown reference; nestimate_no_patterns when no pattern passes the filters; nestimate_no_lme4 when group is set and lme4 is not installed; warning nestimate_missing_outcome when sequences with a missing outcome, covariate or group are dropped; warning nestimate_aliased_pattern when a selected pattern is collinear with the other terms (its row is NA). Warnings from the model fit (e.g. separation) are passed on unchanged.

Details

Steps:

  1. Patterns are found as in sequence_patterns() and filtered by min_freq, min_support, start, end and contain. Patterns absent from all sequences of one outcome value are dropped.

  2. Each pattern gets the chi-square statistic of the number of sequences containing it under each outcome value, against an equal split across the values (codyna's statistic; it does not weight by the size of each outcome group).

  3. The top n patterns by priority enter one model, outcome ~ adjust + pattern_1 + ... + pattern_n, as presence indicators (or occurrence counts with occurrences = TRUE). With group, a random intercept per group is added (lme4::glmer).

The patterns are chosen by their association with the outcome in the same data the model is fitted to, so the p-values do not account for that selection and overstate the evidence. Treat them as a ranking, or confirm the selected patterns on new data.

References

Saqr, M., Tikka, S., & López-Pernas, S. (2026). codyna: Complex Dynamic Systems. R package version 1.0.0.

See also

sequence_patterns
